facts.fact: The paper introduces KAZE features, a novel multiscale 2D feature detection and description algorithm in nonlinear scale spaces.
facts.supporting_span: we introduce KAZE features , a novel multiscale 2D feature detection and description algorithm in nonlinear scale spaces .

facts.fact: Previous approaches detect and describe features at different scale levels by building or approximating the Gaussian scale space of an image.
facts.supporting_span: Previous approaches detect and describe features at different scale levels by building or approximating the Gaussian scale space of an image .

facts.fact: Gaussian blurring does not respect the natural boundaries of objects.
facts.supporting_span: Gaussian blurring does not respect the natural boundaries of objects

facts.fact: Gaussian blurring smoothes to the same degree both details and noise.
facts.supporting_span: smoothes to the same degree both details and noise

facts.fact: Gaussian blurring reduces localization accuracy and distinctiveness.
2D features are detected and described in a nonlinear scale space by means of nonlinear diffusion filtering.
facts.supporting_span: we detect and describe 2D features in a nonlinear scale space by means of nonlinear diffusion filtering .

facts.fact: Blurring can be made locally adaptive to the image data.
facts.supporting_span: we can make blurring locally adaptive to the image data

facts.fact: Locally adaptive blurring retains object boundaries.
Locally adaptive blurring obtains superior localization accuracy and distinctiviness.
facts.supporting_span: obtaining superior localization accuracy and distinctiviness .

facts.fact: The nonlinear scale space is built using efficient Additive Operator Splitting (AOS) techniques and variable con-ductance diffusion.
facts.supporting_span: The nonlinear scale space is built using efficient Additive Operator Splitting (AOS) techniques and variable con-ductance diffusion .

facts.fact: An extensive evaluation on benchmark datasets is presented.

facts.fact: A practical matching application on deformable surfaces is presented.

facts.fact: KAZE features are somewhat more expensive to compute than SURF due to the construction of the nonlinear scale space.
